description: Replace the traditional finite-state-machine (FSM) approach to CSV parsing with a data-flow graph where structural indices (bitmasks) flow through transformation stages. This decouples the parsing pipeline into independent stages that can be software-pipelined and parallelized, eliminating branch-heavy control flow.
mathematical_formalization: Traditional FSM: state_{i+1} = delta(state_i, input_i), sequential chain of N. Dataflow: Stage1 -> Stage2 -> Stage3 -> Stage4, each processing W bytes independently. Pipeline throughput: T = min(T_stage_k). Improvement: W / C_fsm_per_byte.
analogical_connections: CPU 5-stage RISC pipeline: bitmasks are data flowing between stages
Stream processing (Kafka/Flink): each stage is a stream operator
Signal processing filter chains: cascaded processing of data blocks
implementation_hypothesis: 4 pipeline stages: (1) classify_block -> bitmasks, (2) resolve_quotes -> in_string mask, (3) apply_mask -> effective delimiters, (4) extract_fields -> column data. Software-pipeline blocks through these stages.
experiment_seed: Compare FSM parser vs. pipelined dataflow parser. Measure ILP via perf counters. Profile stage balance. Target: IPC > 3.0.
